title: Surface area, or surface area ↔ volume
subtitle: Area and volume · 7 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **7 of the official questions in Area and volume are this one** — 0 Easy, 1 Medium, 6 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- Either you get a box's three dimensions and must find the total area of its faces, or you get a cube's surface area and must find its volume (or the reverse).

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) For a box, surface area = 2(lw + lh + wh).
- 2) If you need to go from surface area to volume, divide by 6, take the square root to get s, then cube it.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Type 2(lw+lh+wh) with the numbers substituted to check.
For a cube chain, solving 6x² = SA and then cubing x is fast.
It is only an arithmetic check.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You may count only three faces instead of six.
For a cube, you may divide the surface area by 6 and give that as the volume, or skip the square root and cube the wrong number.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
